````text
## What changed and why

When a pull request introduces balance or behavior changes to a card, scripted e2e tests that rely on fixed decks and shuffles may break (e.g., changes to cost or health that prevent an expected card play or survival). Previously, pull requests only ran the fixed six `SMOKE` browser tests, leaving failures to be uncovered on main during the daily super run and blocking promotions.

This change:
1. Adds `jackioh changed-cards [--root <dir>] [--json]` to [crates/tools/src/changed.rs](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-5099/crates/tools/src/changed.rs) and [crates/tools/src/main.rs](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-5099/crates/tools/src/main.rs), with its command row documented in [crates/tools/README.md](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-5099/crates/tools/README.md). It reports the card IDs changed in a PR's two-parent merge commit (`changed_cards`). When `HEAD` is not a two-parent merge commit (on main, in the squash merge queue, or local branch) or the base commit cannot be fetched, it returns an empty ID list with an explanatory note and exits 0 (preventing fragments fallback from claiming unrelated pending cards).
2. Updates [e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-5099/e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs) for `--smoke` sharding. When the `jackioh` release binary exists (or at `JACKIOH_BIN`), it queries `changed-cards --json`. It then identifies all specs that quote a changed card's ID or catalog name ("names"), or quote a fixture deck in `fixtures/decks/*.json` that includes a changed card ("deals"). Specs naming a card take priority over deck-dealt specs, ordered lightest first by `WEIGHTS` (file name tie-breaker). Specs are added up to a budget of `SMOKE_EXTRA_BUDGET_S = 120` seconds per shard (e.g. 480 s over 4 shards). Any specs past budget are logged to stderr as left to the daily run; specs 46 and 47 are strictly excluded per #4092.
3. Documents smoke selection behavior in [e2e/README.md](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-5099/e2e/README.md).
4. Adds unit and CLI coverage in [apps/web/src/net/e2e-smoke-selection.test.ts](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-5099/apps/web/src/net/e2e-smoke-selection.test.ts).
````

````text
# #5099: Patch: a pull request that changes a card also runs the e2e specs whose seeded games deal or name that card, within a time cap
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Several browser tests play scripted games with fixed decks and a fixed shuffle: a set number of turns, playing particular cards in particular slots. When a balance change alters a card those games rely on (its cost, its health, a new keyword), the script stops working. A card no longer fits in the mana left, or a unit survives that the test expects to die. Today a pull request runs only six of these browser tests, so the balance change merges green and the break shows up the next morning in the daily run. That red daily run holds the staging site and production promotion until the night bot fixes the test.

Once this is built, a pull request that changes a card also runs the few browser tests whose decks hold that card or that name it, up to a fixed time budget. In most cases the author sees the broken test on their own pull request and fixes it there, rather than it landing on main. Example: the change that made Professor Curvature 4/5 would have run the Tesla trap test on its own pull request and failed there, instead of in the next day's run.

## Why

A card change breaking a seeded e2e spec that only the daily run plays has happened six times since mid-October, three of them in the last three days:

- #4654 (2026-11-24): #4440 made core-077 Professor Curvature 4/5, and spec 29 (`29-animated-trap.cy.ts`, `cy.handCardByName("Professor Curvature")`, deck fixture `03-plays-a`) expected it to die to Tesla.
- #4800 (2026-11-24): #4665 made core-026 Glowy Jelly Bean Tradable. It was filler in both `08-reserves-*.json` decks, so R82 never ended a turn and spec 08 failed.
- #5029 (2026-11-26): #4897's cards dealt tutorial lesson 5's coach a Cloaked card, and spec 48's helper could not answer its picker.
- #2361: #2220 made core-081 Radiant Saintess cost (2), and spec 03 (`cy.playByName("Radiant Saintess")`, `03-plays-a`) could no longer play it.
- #2719: #2662 cut core-028 to 1 mana, and spec 11 (deck `11-radiant-a`, three cards including core-028) failed in daily e2e shard 5.
- #1237: core-093 Combo-Index went to cost 3, and spec 28 (`const COMBO_INDEX = "Combo-Index"`, deck `28-combo-a`) failed in daily e2e (5/8).

Each one turned the daily super run red. Since #3278 and #3656, production promotes only from a green super run of staging, and staging holds while that run is red. On 2026-11-25 the owner made the same call for fuzz: the merge queue's fuzz slice (`scripts/fuzz-slice.sh`) exists so that "a change that breaks a fuzz invariant leaves the queue instead of turning the next daily run red". Nothing does this for e2e. `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs` `SMOKE` is a fixed six specs (01, 06, 10, 13, 19, 51), whatever the pull request changes.

The pieces already exist:

- `crates/tools/src/changed.rs` `changed_cards` already reads a pull request's changed cards from its merge commit. It counts scripts whose code moved and catalog entries changed in a field that plays (not `WORDING_FIELDS`), and fetches the base when the checkout is shallow. The fuzz gate uses it today.
- Every e2e shard job already unpacks `target/release/jackioh` (`.github/actions/e2e-shard`).
- The shard job picks its specs with `node scripts/shard-specs.mjs --smoke k K`. `scripts/ci-shards.toml`'s header says the bot may change that script.

Measured cost, from `/tmp` scripts over the 45 fixtures in `e2e/fixtures/decks/` and the spec sources:

- 103 cards appear in some spec's fixture decks, and 51 cards are named (quoted name or id) by some spec.
- In the last two weeks, 14 of the 35 commits that changed `catalog.json` touched one of those cards.
- A card named by specs pulls in a median of 1 spec (72 s by `WEIGHTS`), at most 8 (362 s).
- A card held in fixtures pulls in a median of 9 specs (360 s), at most 34. That is why a cap is needed.
- Under the cap and ordering proposed below, the rule would have caught 4 of the 6 breaks above (specs 03, 11, 28 and 29). Spec 08 (170 s, behind lighter specs) and spec 48 (tutorial decks, not fixtures) would still be left to the daily run.

## Proposal

1. **A `jackioh changed-cards [--json]` subcommand** that prints `changed_cards(root)`'s ids and notes. It prints no ids (and says why) when `HEAD` is not a two-parent merge commit or the base cannot be read. This matters because in the squash merge queue and on main, the fragments-only fallback would name every pending fragment's cards.
2. **`shard-specs.mjs --smoke` adds specs for changed cards.** When `../target/release/jackioh` exists, it calls that subcommand. It then adds every spec that either loads a fixture deck holding a changed card (the fixture id as a string literal in the spec) or names a changed card (its quoted catalog name or id).
3. **Order and cap.** Specs that name a changed card come first, then the rest, lightest first by `WEIGHTS`, each order tie broken by file name. They are added until the extra weight would pass a named budget of 120 s per shard (480 s over today's four). Every shard computes the same list. The specs over budget are printed as left to the daily run.
4. **Specs 46 and 47 never join (#4092).** Nothing changes when no card changed, in the merge queue, on main or in a local run without the binary.
5. **Logging.** The smoke log prints the changed cards and the specs they added, so a failure says why the spec ran.

Why the 120 s cap: today's heaviest smoke shard carries 82 s by `WEIGHTS`. When two shards each carried about 285 s, they ran 8m 7s and 8m 57s (#3764, `ci-shards.toml`). So about 200 s per shard stays inside the job's 10-minute timeout and near the eight-minute aim.

Decisions the issue settles, with the rejected alternative:

- Pull requests only, not the merge queue. A squash queue commit has one parent, so `changed_cards` has no diff there, and the pull request gives the author the failure earlier.
- Fixtures and names, not every spec, and capped. Running every spec on card pull requests would undo #4092's time budget.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/main.rs`, `crates/tools/src/changed.rs` (the subcommand and its JSON, with tests), `crates/tools/README.md` (its row in the command table).
- `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs` (the selection, the cap constant, and the spec-to-card map built from `e2e/fixtures/decks/*.json` and the spec sources), `e2e/README.md` (what the smoke list adds).
- A vitest test of the selection beside `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`.
- No change under `.github/`, `bot/` or `scripts/ci-shards.toml`; the shard count stays 4.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `jackioh changed-cards --json` on a merge commit whose second parent changes core-077's health in `catalog.json` lists `core-077`.
- [ ] On a single-parent commit, or when the base cannot be fetched, it lists no ids and exits 0 with a note saying why.
- [ ] A test: with `core-077` changed, the smoke selection includes `29-animated-trap.cy.ts` and `03-trap-opponent-turn.cy.ts` alongside the six `SMOKE` specs.
- [ ] A test: with `core-093` changed, it includes `28-patch-011-ui.cy.ts`.
- [ ] A test: with no changed cards, the selection is exactly `SMOKE`.
- [ ] A test: with a change that touches many fixture cards (for example core-025), the extra specs' `WEIGHTS` total at most the budget times the shard count. Named specs come before fixture-only ones. The specs over the cap are reported.
- [ ] A test: across k = 1..K, every selected spec lands in exactly one shard, and 46 and 47 are never added.
- [ ] `node scripts/shard-specs.mjs --smoke 1 4` without the binary prints today's shard 1.
- [ ] The tools README table's drift check in `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs` passes with the new row.

## Size and risks

Medium: about 250 lines across one new subcommand, the selection logic and their tests.

Risks:

- Card pull requests whose cards the specs hold run longer e2e smoke shards, up to about two minutes per shard; others run as today.
- `WEIGHTS` are estimates for some specs, and an unlisted spec counts 30 s, so a shard can run somewhat past what the cap predicts.
- A spec already broken on main now also fails the card pull requests that select it, as a broken smoke spec does today.
- Mapping by fixture membership over-selects (filler cards), and by name under-selects: spec 08's filler break and spec 48's tutorial deals stay daily-only.

## Risks

- **Shards must agree.** Each shard job runs `changed-cards` itself (the base is fetched `--depth=1` over the checkout's credentials, as the fuzz job does). If one fetch fails, that shard sees `SMOKE` alone and deals differently, so an extra spec could land on no shard. It is logged, and the daily run still plays it. Accepted: no shared artifact is added.
- **Time.** A core-077-style change adds up to 480 s over 4 shards (about 200 s a shard). `WEIGHTS` are estimates and an unlisted spec counts 30 s, so a shard can run past the prediction. The job timeout is 10 minutes.
- **Over- and under-selection.** Fixture membership pulls in filler-card specs. Names miss specs that reach a card another way (specs 08 and 48 stay daily). Quoted names in spec comments count; accepted.
- A spec already broken on `main` now fails the card pull requests that select it, as a broken smoke spec does today.
- `changed_cards` is unchanged, so the fuzz gate behaves as before; no pure crate is touched.
````
